stem: A team rotates workers between trimming and hand pruning, but both tasks involve similar repetitive grip force. What should the supervisor conclude?
choices: Any rotation automatically provides ergonomic recovery
Rotation is unnecessary whenever tools are sharp
The rotation may not meaningfully change exposure and should be redesigned around different demands
The workers should simply switch tasks more frequently
rationale: Rotation reduces exposure only when the alternate task meaningfully changes the force, posture, repetition, or body-region demands.
